item.title: BU track and field athletes claim BU failed to adequately support team amid Zac Segal controversy
item.description: Multiple members of the Boston University track and field team claimed administrators failed to adequately support them following nationwide backlash sparked by a controversial social media post from teammate and BU College Republicans president Zac Segal.

item.description: Following last week’s record-breaking snowstorm and ongoing freezing temperatures, Boston residents are left to navigate icy, dangerous sidewalk conditions throughout the city. item.title: ‘We’re Bostonians, we’re tough.’ City, MBTA prepare for upcoming World Cup games
item.description: The Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority and Gillette Stadium are preparing for an influx of fans from all over the world this summer, as the Foxborough stadium will host seven FIFA World Cup matches. The preparations include renovations to the Foxboro Commuter Rail station, upgrades to the stadium to fit FIFA standards and enhanced public safety...

item.title: This year’s men’s March Madness will be the best one yet
item.description: The calendar has officially flipped to February — which, for basketball fans, means March Madness is just around the corner. The 68-team, single-elimination college basketball tournament famously operates like a battle royale, with colleges from across the country facing off for a chance at basketball immortality.

item.title: ICE needs melting — and not the frozen kind | The Anti-Imperialist Club
item.description: Immigrants are not the “invaders” ICE paints them to be. They are your neighbors, your coworkers and your friends. With the exception of Indigenous Americans, we all come from immigrants — whether it be our parents, grandparents or an ancestor generations back.

item.title: ‘It really is disappointing.’ BU’s summer journalism high school program canceled, again
item.description: Boston University’s Summer Journalism Academy program has been canceled for the summer of 2026 due to a lack of profitability, said the program’s former director, Burton Glass. This is the second consecutive year the program has been cancelled. The program provided high school students with the opportunity to live on campus for three weeks and learn journalistic skills from BU professors.
